pharm: Antiseizure agent with high, selective affinity for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A); rapidly and completely absorbed, CYP-minor metabolism; Schedule V controlled substance.
quick: 50 mg PO/IV twice daily (range 25-100 mg BID)
With or without food (high-fat meal slows but does not reduce absorption)
May cause fetal harm (animal data); enroll in AED registry
No adjustment (not recommended in end-stage renal disease)
Reduce dose for all stages of hepatic impairment
summary: Brivaracetam is an antiepileptic for partial-onset (focal) seizures in patients 1 month and older, available as tablets, oral solution, and IV (interchangeable). It binds synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) with high selectivity. The usual starting dose is 50 mg twice daily, titratable to 25-100 mg twice daily; no gradual escalation is required. Key cautions are suicidal ideation/behavior (AED class effect), somnolence/dizziness, psychiatric/behavioral reactions, and rare hypersensitivity (bronchospasm, angioedema). It is a Schedule V controlled substance and requires dose reduction in hepatic impairment.
indications: Treatment of partial-onset (focal) seizures in patients 1 month of age and older (monotherapy or adjunctive)

dosage.n: Adjust between 25 and 100 mg twice daily (50-200 mg/day) per response/tolerability; no gradual escalation required

dosage.d: Start 25 mg twice daily; max 75 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Dose reduction recommended for any degree of hepatic impairment
Rifampin induces CYP2C19, lowering brivaracetam levels

admin: Tablets, oral solution, and IV injection are interchangeable at the same dose
IV may be given as a bolus or infusion when oral administration is temporarily not feasible
May be taken with or without food
No gradual dose escalation is required when starting
Withdraw gradually (do not stop abruptly) to reduce the risk of increased seizures/status epilepticus
moa: The precise anticonvulsant mechanism is not fully known; brivaracetam displays high and selective affinity for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) in the brain, which is thought to modulate neurotransmitter release and contribute to its antiseizure effect.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to brivaracetam or any inactive ingredient (bronchospasm and angioedema have occurred)
relative: History of psychiatric disorders or suicidal ideation

preg: Based on animal data, brivaracetam may cause fetal harm (increased embryofetal mortality and decreased fetal body weights). Human data are insufficient. Encourage enrollment in the North American Antiepileptic Drug (NAAED) Pregnancy Registry (1-888-233-2334).
lact: Data on human milk excretion are limited; a decision to breastfeed should weigh developmental/health benefits against the mother's clinical need and potential infant effects.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for renal impairment; brivaracetam is not recommended in patients with end-stage renal disease undergoing dialysis (not studied). Less than 10% is excreted unchanged in urine.
hepatic: Dose reduction is recommended for ALL stages of hepatic impairment - start at 25 mg twice daily with a maximum of 75 mg twice daily.

major: Rifampin (CYP2C19 inducer) - decreases brivaracetam levels; increase dose up to 100%
moderate: Carbamazepine (brivaracetam may raise carbamazepine-epoxide; reduce carbamazepine if tolerability issues)
Phenytoin (brivaracetam can raise phenytoin levels - monitor)
Other CNS depressants and alcohol (additive sedation)
minor: Levetiracetam (no added therapeutic benefit when combined)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal slows absorption but does not change the extent absorbed.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor phenytoin levels when co-administered; no routine brivaracetam level monitoring required.

serious: Suicidal behavior and ideation (AED class effect)
Psychiatric reactions (irritability, depression, aggression, anxiety, psychotic symptoms)
rare: Withdrawal seizures/status epilepticus on abrupt discontinuation

monitoring: Emergence or worsening of depression, suicidal thoughts, or behavior changes
Somnolence, fatigue, and ability to drive/operate machinery
Signs of hypersensitivity (rash, swelling, breathing difficulty)
counsel: Take twice daily, with or without food; you can start at the target dose without slow titration
Do not stop suddenly - this can trigger more seizures; your doctor will taper it
Watch for and report any new or worsening depression, mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm
It may cause drowsiness or dizziness - avoid driving until you know how it affects you, and avoid alcohol
Seek emergency care for swelling of the face/throat, wheezing, or trouble breathing
This is a controlled medicine - keep it secure and do not share it
pk: Rapid absorption; antiseizure effect over titration period
Store at controlled room temperature per labeling
pearls: Binds SV2A with ~15-30x higher affinity than levetiracetam and crosses into the brain rapidly
No therapeutic benefit from combining with levetiracetam (same target)
No gradual titration needed - can start at an effective dose
Dose reduction is required for any hepatic impairment; no renal adjustment but avoid in ESRD
Schedule V controlled substance; class-wide suicidality warning applies
Tablets, oral solution, and IV are interchangeable at equal doses
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the regular twice-daily schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Limited experience; reported effects include somnolence, dizziness, vertigo, balance disorder, fatigue, nausea, diplopia, anxiety, and bradycardia. No specific antidote. Provide standard supportive care, secure airway/oxygenation/ventilation, and monitor cardiac rhythm and vital signs. Hemodialysis is not expected to enhance clearance (<10% renal excretion).
